nodes.name: Hydrothermal CoFe LDH synthesis
nodes.procedure: CoFe LDH/NF was synthesized by hydrothermally treating a mixture of 3 mmol Co(NO3)2·6H2O, 1 mmol Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, and 5 mmol urea in 30 ml deionized water with a pre-cleaned 2×3 cm² NF at 120°C for 10 h. The product was rinsed with deionized water and ethanol, then dried at 60°C, and shows a loading of ~1.65 mg cm^-2.

nodes.name: PW12-POM docking
nodes.procedure: PW12-CoFe LDH/NF was obtained via 30 min immersion of hydrothermally grown CoFe LDH/NF in 1 mM PW12-POM aqueous solution, followed by drying at 60°C. PW12-CoFe LDH/NF shows a loading of ~1.94 mg cm^-2.

nodes.source_text: The engineered PW12-POM-docked CoFe layered double hydroxide on Ni foam (ΔPW12-CoFe LDH/NF) anode was fabricated by submerging hydrothermally grown CoFe LDH/NF in an aqueous PW12·POM solution... POM-CoFe LDH/NF was obtained via 30 min immersion in 1 mM POM solution (PW12-POM...), followed by drying at 60°C. PW12-CoFe LDH/NF shows a loading of ~1.94 mg cm^-2

nodes.procedure: RuO2/NF electrode was prepared following previously reported work, in which commercially available RuO2 powders were uniformly deposited onto pre-cleaned NF with a mass loading identical to that of CoFe LDH/NF.

nodes.description: OER LSV evaluation in 1 M KOH with 100% iR correction
nodes.source_text: PW₁₂-CoFe LDH/NF achieves current densities of 100, 500, and 1000 mA cm⁻² at overpotentials of 265, 325, and 368 mV, respectively, outperforming CoFe LDH/NF, which requires 285, 372, and 458 mV

nodes.description: Chronopotentiometry stability at 1 A/cm² in alkaline seawater without iR correction
nodes.source_text: PW₁₂-CoFe LDH/NF remains stable for over 1300 hours... achieves ~99.7% Faradaic efficiency for O₂ production... ultraviolet–visible spectroscopy detected only trace active chlorine

nodes.description: MEA electrolyzer stability at 1 A/cm² in alkaline seawater at 60°C and 80°C

nodes.description: OER LSV and stability comparison in 1 M KOH and alkaline seawater
nodes.source_text: CoFe LDH/NF, which requires 285, 372, and 458 mV to attain the same benchmarks... deactivates after 60 hours... markedly high levels for CoFe LDH/NF after 60 hours

nodes.description: Chronopotentiometry stability at 2 A/cm² in alkaline seawater without iR correction
nodes.source_text: At a higher current density of 2.0 A cm⁻², PW₁₂·CoFe LDH/NF can maintain stable operation for over 600 hours
Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy tests... confirms the much lower charge transfer resistance... smaller phase angle of PW₁₂-CoFe LDH/NF implies more charges are engaged in Faradaic processes

nodes.characterization_summary: Both CoFe LDH/NF and PW12-CoFe LDH/NF exhibit identical Bragg reflections matching hexagonal-phase LDH (PDF#50-0235) with no shift at 11.7° for (003) plane, confirming surface binding rather than intercalation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of CoFe LDH/NF and PW12-CoFe LDH/NF exhibit identical Bragg reflections in alignment with the hexagonal-phase LDH (PDF#50-0235, Fig. 1a).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show CoFe LDH nanosheets aligned perpendicularly with PW12-POM incorporation leaving morphology unchanged.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images show that CoFe LDH nanosheets are aligned perpendicularly, with PW12-POM incorporation leaving their morphology unchanged (Supplementary Fig. 1 and Fig. 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping and EDX spectrum verify uniform distribution of Co, Fe, P, W, and O throughout the NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mapping images and energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectrum analysis verify the existence of Co, Fe, P, W, and O throughout the NF (Supplementary Fig. 2).

nodes.characterization_summary: P/W ratio of ~1:13.1 consistent with PW12-POM stoichiometry, PW12-POM accounts for 36.6 wt% of PW12-CoFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) analysis further demonstrates a P/W ratio of ~ 1:13.1, closely consistent with PW12-POM stoichiometry, and PW12-POM accounts for 36.6 wt% of PW12-CoFe LDH (Supplementary Table 1).

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM confirms PW12-CoFe LDH nanosheet is ~3 nm thick.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic force microscopy image confirms that the PW12-CoFe LDH nanosheet is ∼3 nm thick (Supplementary Fig. 3).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM displays orderly stacked ultrathin nanosheets of PW12-CoFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image of PW12-CoFe LDH further displays the orderly stacked ultrathin nanosheets (Fig. 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-STEM images indicate nanoclusters on CoFe LDH (012) plane with structural details matching PW12-POM molecule configuration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-STEM) images (Supplementary Fig. 4 and Fig. 1d) indicate the presence of nanoclusters on the CoFe LDH (012) plane.

properties.description: TEM image showing nanoparticles with circular features and scale bar

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows PW12-POM induces slight shifts in Co 2p and marked shifts in Fe 2p toward higher binding energies for PW12-CoFe LDH, with shifts toward lower binding energies in W 4f and P 2p regions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) spectra in the Co 2p and Fe 2p regions reveals that the introduction of PW12-POM induces slight shifts in Co 2p and marked shifts in Fe 2p toward higher binding energies, as well as shifts toward lower binding energies in the W 4f and P 2p regions (Supplementary Fig. 5).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show intensified terminal W=O asymmetric stretching vibration relative to symmetric stretching, indicative of robust coordination between PW12-POM and CoFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra shown in Supplementary Fig. 7 show the signals of PW12-POM, particularly with the intensified terminal W=O asymmetric stretching vibration relative to the W=O symmetric stretching vibration...

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge shifts to higher energy and Co K-edge shows slight shift in PW12-CoFe LDH vs CoFe LDH; average oxidation states are Fe 3.51 and Co 2.34 vs 2.62 and 2.13 in CoFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy was applied... the average oxidation states of Fe and Co in PW12-CoFe LDH are 3.51 and 2.34, respectively, higher than those in CoFe LDH (2.62 and 2.13).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge EXAFS shows increased Fe-O bond intensity at 1.5 Å, Fe-O-Co bond positive shift at 2.5 Å indicating Fe-O-W formation; Co K-edge shows minimal change.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) analysis of the Fe K-edge reveals an increase in the relative intensity of the Fe–O bond at 1.5 Å in PW12-CoFe LDH compared to CoFe LDH (Fig. 1k)...

nodes.characterization_summary: TOF-SIMS mapping after 24h electrolysis shows both electrodes covered with OH⁻ but weaker Cl⁻ signal on PW12-CoFe LDH/NF vs CoFe LDH/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) was employed... TOF-SIMS mapping images reveal that both electrodes are predominantly covered with OH⁻. However, the Cl⁻ signal on PW12-CoFe LDH/NF is markedly weaker...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows metal oxyhydroxides formation at lower potentials for PW12-CoFe LDH/NF vs CoFe LDH/NF, indicated by increased intensity ratio of 452.6 and 526.3 cm⁻¹ peaks and new peak at 1060 cm⁻¹ for –OOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Raman spectroscopy was further conducted... Remarkably, this structural transformation occurs at lower potentials for PW12-CoFe LDH/NF than for CoFe LDH/NF...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Co K-edge shows faster shift to higher energy for PW12-CoFe LDH vs CoFe LDH; Fe K-edge remains stable for PW12-CoFe LDH but shifts positively for CoFe LDH during ASO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further elucidate the catalytic mechanism, we conducted in situ XAS tests... The Co K-edge for PW12-CoFe LDH exhibits a faster and more pronounced shift to higher energy compared to CoFe LDH (Fig. 3e)...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Fe K-edge EXAFS shows stable Fe–O bond length and coordination number for PW12-CoFe LDH across potentials vs bond elongation and reduced coordination for CoFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EXAFS fitting reveals that the Fe–O bond length and coordination number remain nearly constant for PW12-CoFe LDH across the applied potentials... (Fig. 3f).
